newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva police detain Nigerian rights activist.
newsitem.headline: Geneva police detain Nigerian rights activist.

text.p: Geneva police have detained a Nigerian activist attending the U.N. human rights forum after Swiss saleswomen at a high street boutique accused him of stealing dresses, U.N. sources and activists said on Friday.

In an embarrassing incident for the Swiss hosts of the main annual United Nations rights meeting, Clement Nwankwo, head of a non-governmental agency in Lagos, was arrested on Saturday after two saleswomen at the shop informed the police, they said.

U.N. sources and human rights activists said Nwankwo had been convicted of theft on Tuesday and sentenced to 20 days in jail, which was suspended pending appeal. They said he was held incommunicado for four days despite his request to see a lawyer.

In a statement, he alleged brutal treatment by police in the international city and accused them of racism. He said he was beaten by the police, stripped naked while in custody and not allowed to make phone calls.
Nwankwo's lawyer Olivier Cramer told Swiss news agency ATS that the court had ordered the activist expelled and not to enter Switzerland for three years.
He said police arrested his client despite failing to find on him the clothes he was alleged to have stolen.
Geneva police spokesman Emile Berthod denied the Nigerian's charges. He said cantonal justice chief Gerard Ramseyer had ordered an administrative investigation into the case.
